scope: Device & materials: oxide-semiconductor DRAM (IGZO/IWO/ITO/In2O3 2T0C/3T0C/1T1C, OCTRAM, display-fab IGZO), ferroelectric memory (HZO FeRAM/FeCAP, FeFET, FTJ, AlScN ferro-diode, PZT F-RAM, Micron NVDRAM, FMC DRAM+), and 3D DRAM (NEO 3D X-DRAM, IDM roadmaps, 3D NOR).

cards.name: OS-eDRAM: IGZO/IWO 2T0C gain-cell memory IP on a U.S. 200mm foundry
cards.what_it_is: A fabless IP company co-develops a low-temperature (<400C) IGZO or W-doped In2O3 2T0C gain-cell BEOL module with SkyWater (S130 in Bloomington MN, or the ex-Infineon Fab 25 in Austin, 130-65nm, 200mm). It then licenses the memory macro and compiler to ASIC designers, giving them on-die memory with ~4-5x the bit density of 130nm SRAM and near-zero standby leakage, stacked over logic.
cards.why_it_could_work: IGZO off-current ~3e-19 A/um gives >400-1,000 s retention (imec IEDM 2020/2021) vs SRAM's constant leakage, so an always-on edge chip can hold weights/activations at near-zero standby power. A planar 2T0C at ~30F2 is ~0.5 um2/bit at 130nm vs ~2.0-2.5 um2 for 6T SRAM [ESTIMATE], and because it sits in BEOL it uses no extra silicon area. Arbitrage: SkyWater bought Fab 25 (~$73M + working capital, ~400k wafer starts/yr) and is converting it to a foundry, so it needs differentiated process options. Embedded-memory IP royalties carry ~85% gross margin.

cards.time_to_first_revenue_text: 36-48 months: 12-18 mo module development with foundry, 12 mo test chip + reliability, then first NRE/license from an edge-AI or defense ASIC customer
cards.us_manufacturability: SkyWater Bloomington MN (S130/S90) or SkyWater Fab 25 Austin TX (130-65nm), both 200mm; needs a new IGZO sputter or In2O3 ALD + O2 anneal module. Development could start at NY CREATES Albany (300mm) or Purdue (200mm oxide BEOL demonstrated Sep 2026).
cards.who_is_already_doing_this: imec (2T0C program since IEDM 2020), Kioxia, IMECAS, Macronix (3D 2T0C), Georgia Tech/Shimeng Yu (IWO eDRAM), Notre Dame/Datta (IWO 2T), Purdue/Ye & Li (ALD In2O3 3-layer 200mm), SEL (DOSRAM / OS-LSI; dominant oxide-semiconductor patent estate). Competing embedded memories already at U.S. foundries: Weebit ReRAM (SkyWater S130), MRAM at GlobalFoundries.
cards.wins_axis: standby power per bit (W/Mb at idle) and on-die memory density vs SRAM at mature nodes
cards.buyer: Always-on edge-AI ASICs (keyword spotting, vision wake-up, sensor fusion) and DoD/onshore sensor ASICs on 130-65nm U.S. nodes that are SRAM-limited
cards.glut_reason: Priced against on-die SRAM/MRAM/ReRAM, not DDR5; a DDR5 price collapse does not change an ASIC's on-die memory choice.
cards.fatal_flaw: No U.S. foundry offers an oxide-semiconductor module. Qualifying one costs ~$10-30M and 3+ years [ESTIMATE], and PBTI lifetime was only ~1 year vs a 5-10 year target (imec 2021). ASIC teams rarely design in a single-source, unqualified memory when SkyWater already offers qualified ReRAM. SEL's patent estate is a freedom-to-operate risk.
cards.business_model_lenses: IP licensing; fabless->foundry; university/lab patent license (Georgia Tech/Notre Dame IWO, Purdue In2O3); defense-first
cards.founder_fit_note: Not as a solo founder: needs a device/process CTO and a SkyWater JDA. The founder could own BD and the software side (memory compiler GUI, characterization data portal).
cards.possible: yes - cells demonstrated on 300mm, oxide BEOL demonstrated on a U.S. 200mm line (Purdue)
cards.profitable: marginal - royalties on low-volume 130nm ASICs are small; the real money needs a 28nm-or-better foundry partner
cards.doable_by_founder: no - process-module development and reliability qualification are far beyond <$50k and a day job

cards.name: Standalone IGZO 2T0C DRAM die on a depreciated U.S. 200mm line (commodity DRAM substitute)
cards.what_it_is: Build discrete DRAM-substitute chips (DDR4/LPDDR-class interface) from four stacked IGZO 2T0C tiers over CMOS periphery on a depreciated U.S. 200mm 130nm line (SkyWater Fab 25 Austin) and sell them into the 2026 shortage. A capacitor-less, BEOL-stackable cell on cheap wafers is the whole pitch.
cards.why_it_could_work: No capacitor, low-temperature BEOL, and stackable tiers (IMECAS showed 4-layer 3D 2T0C with 400 s retention and 3 bits/cell at VLSI 2026), with depreciated 200mm wafers at ~$1-2.5K [ESTIMATE], while DDR5 sells for ~$27/GB. The scratch model kills it: ~0.0035 Gb/mm2 => ~7.6 GB per 200mm wafer => ~$336/GB including test and packaging, ~12x today's DDR5 price, ~31x the glut price and ~125x DDR5's estimated cost (~$2.7/GB). Even a hypothetical 300mm 28nm-class 4-tier version models at ~$11.8/GB, about the glut price and ~4x DRAM cost, and no U.S. foundry offers that line.

cards.us_manufacturability: SkyWater Fab 25 Austin (200mm, 130-65nm) technically could add IGZO tiers; 130nm litho is the binding constraint
cards.who_is_already_doing_this: Nobody commercially at mature nodes; imec, IMECAS, Kioxia, SK hynix, and Samsung pursue oxide DRAM at leading-edge pitches
cards.wins_axis: none for commodity buyers (loses on $/GB, bandwidth, latency); refresh power only

cards.glut_reason: Already ~12x DDR5's current price; in a glut where DDR5 falls 60% toward ~$11/GB the gap widens to ~31x.
cards.fatal_flaw: 130nm lithography gives ~120x lower bit density than 1b DRAM (0.0035 vs 0.436 Gb/mm2 with 4 tiers); stacking recovers only linear factors.
cards.founder_fit_note: No: T3 capital, process engineering, and a product that loses on cost by an order of magnitude.
cards.possible: yes - physics works (2T0C cells and 4-tier stacks are demonstrated)
cards.profitable: no - $/GB 12x DDR5 price today, ~125x DDR5 cost

cards.name: IGZO memory printed on idle display-fab glass
cards.what_it_is: Use a depreciated Gen 6-8.5 oxide-TFT display backplane line (the CAAC-IGZO process Sharp and SEL commercialized) to pattern 2T0C memory arrays on glass, then cut and bond them to silicon sense/IO chips as cheap bulk memory. Large-area tooling and a 4-6 mask process are the 'cheaper process/capital' bet.
cards.why_it_could_work: Display oxide-TFT lines are heavily depreciated and running underutilized (Omdia 2025). IGZO TFT leakage is tiny (SEL CAAC-IGZO <=200 zA), and a Gen 8.5 sheet is ~5.5 m2. Scratch model: at a ~2 um design rule a 2T0C cell is ~120 um2 => ~4e-6 Gb/mm2 => only ~2.3 GB per sheet => ~$266/GB before bonding, with microsecond access.

cards.name: OCTRAM-class 4F2 IGZO-on-capacitor low-refresh DRAM as a U.S. second source
cards.what_it_is: License Kioxia and Nanya's OCTRAM (a vertical cylindrical InGaZnO access transistor built on top of a high-aspect-ratio DRAM capacitor, 4F2) and have it produced for U.S. low-power DRAM buyers. The product would be a low-refresh LPDDR-class part for defense and IoT.
cards.why_it_could_work: Ioff <1 aA/cell and Ion >15 uA (2024), >30 uA in Kioxia's 8-layer stack (IEDM 2025); a 275 Mbit array works at 54/63nm pitches. Scratch model at demo pitches on a DRAM-class line: ~0.16 Gb/mm2, ~$8.4/GB (below DDR5's ~$27 price but ~3x DDR5's estimated ~$2.7/GB cost at today's demo pitch).

cards.name: License NEO Semiconductor 3D X-DRAM and build it in the U.S.
cards.what_it_is: Take a license to NEO Semiconductor's (San Jose) 3D X-DRAM (1T1C, or 3T0C with IGZO channels), built with a modified 3D-NAND flow, and stand up or partner on a U.S. 3D-NAND-class line to make it. This is the '3D NAND economics for DRAM' bet.
cards.why_it_could_work: NEO claims ~10x DRAM density (up to 512Gb), <10 ns, >1e14 endurance and >1 s retention at 85C (company-reported PoC, Apr 2026). At the claimed density the scratch model gives ~$1.2/GB, which would be transformative if real. The big IDMs are converging on 3D: Samsung 16-tier VS-DRAM (VLSI 2026), SK hynix 5-layer at 56.1% yield (2024, needs 32-192 layers), Kioxia 8-layer IGZO stack, IMECAS 4-layer 2T0C.

cards.name: U.S.-made HZO FeRAM family (1-16 Mb, rad-hard option) via SkyWater + Sandia
cards.what_it_is: A fabless company designs a family of hafnium-zirconium-oxide 1T1C FeRAM chips (SPI/QSPI and parallel, 1-16 Mb, plus rad-hard variants). The HZO capacitor module would be built on SkyWater's 130nm line (Bloomington MN or Fab 25 Austin), with rad-hard variants co-developed with or licensed from Sandia, which integrated HZO FeRAM into its trusted MESA fab at 200mm (May 2026). It sells an onshore second source to Infineon's PZT F-RAM.
cards.why_it_could_work: HZO is ALD-deposited and CMOS-friendly (no PZT lead contamination; ~2-3 extra masks, by analogy to TI's 2-mask FRAM on 130nm) and radiation hard (heavy-ion data; Sandia program). Space/defense F-RAM is close to sole-source (Infineon QML-V 2Mb). Wafers: ~$1,400 per 200mm [ESTIMATE]. This is a supply-security play, not a $/GB play: the scratch model is ~$770/GB because these are Mb-class parts.

cards.wins_axis: supply security (U.S.-made, trusted) + non-volatile fast writes + radiation hardness
cards.buyer: Space/defense primes (satellite bus controllers, munitions/flight data recorders) and industrial/automotive event-data recorders wanting an onshore second source

cards.fatal_flaw: HZO loses to incumbent PZT F-RAM on the specs F-RAM buyers pay for: 1e11 endurance and 1-month retention at 85C (IEDM 2023, 1Mb) vs 1e13-1e14 and >100 years. Infineon's F-RAM is already partly U.S.-fabbed (TI Dallas; Fab 25 history), so 'Made in USA' is not a moat against it. The niche is ~hundreds of $M/yr [ESTIMATE].

cards.profitable: marginal - small, incumbent-dominated niche with a reliability gap to close
cards.doable_by_founder: no - T2 chip company with qualification burden

cards.name: AlScN ferro-diode memory for 500-600C electronics (Penn/AFRL license + STTR)
cards.what_it_is: License Penn's AlScN ferroelectric-diode NVM (Jariwala/Olsson group, co-developed with AFRL) and build kB-to-Mb memory dies and high-temperature packaged modules for SiC electronics. Target uses are hypersonics, turbine-engine health monitoring, downhole geothermal/oil tools and Venus/space probes, entered through AFRL/DARPA SBIR-STTR contracts.
cards.why_it_could_work: Silicon DRAM and flash fail well below 300C [ESTIMATE]. Ni/Al0.68Sc0.32N/Pt diodes switched at 600C for >60 h at <15 V, which is compatible with SiC logic (Nature Electronics 2024), and scaled devices reach >100 Mbit/mm2 (arXiv 2025). The 2-terminal self-rectifying crossbar is a simple 3-4 mask BEOL. DoD keeps asking for this: AF254-D0806 (500C kB-scale NVM manufacturing scale-up) and DARPA DPA26BZ04-DV017 (-269 to +600C NVM, ~$1.2M Direct-to-Phase II, closed Aug 2026).

cards.us_manufacturability: Prototype at Penn's Singh Center for Nanotechnology, Philadelphia [external-user access UNVERIFIED]; scale on a U.S. 200mm line with AlN/AlScN sputter capability (MEMS/RF foundries or SkyWater) [UNVERIFIED which has AlScN today]; high-temperature ceramic packaging from U.S. hybrid houses.

cards.wins_axis: operating temperature / survival in extreme environments (no incumbent RAM or flash works at 500C+)
cards.buyer: AFRL and hypersonic/engine programs; aero-engine OEMs (health monitoring); downhole tool makers (oilfield services, geothermal); planetary-probe teams

cards.fatal_flaw: Tiny, grant-shaped market that easily becomes an SBIR mill (the mission bars grant farming). It also needs a high-temperature periphery (SiC CMOS) that barely exists commercially, and Penn may already have licensed or spun out the IP [UNVERIFIED].

cards.profitable: marginal - high ASP but very low volume; depends on DoD program pull
cards.doable_by_founder: marginal - best founder-entry among device cards via STTR, but not an 18-month revenue path

cards.why_it_could_work: NVDRAM promised near-DRAM speed with non-volatility; at DRAM-like density the scratch model gives ~$4/GB if a DRAM maker built it. High DRAM prices revive interest in cheaper tiers.

cards.fatal_flaw: Needs a DRAM fab plus a CPU/OS ecosystem. Optane lost ~$576M in 2020 alone and took a $559M impairment, and the one company able to build NVDRAM (Micron) never productized it.
cards.profitable: no - market rejected the tier at Optane's cost; startup has no fab

cards.name: U.S. design-in and module partner for FMC DRAM+ (HfO2 non-volatile DRAM)
cards.what_it_is: Become FMC's U.S. application channel: eval boards, reference designs and small-volume non-volatile memory modules (U.S.-assembled at an East Coast EMS) around FMC's DRAM+ (ferroelectric HfO2 replacing the DRAM capacitor). Customers would be U.S. industrial PLC, medical-device and automotive data-logging OEMs.
cards.why_it_could_work: FMC raised EUR100M (Nov 2025) with two DRAM-maker partners and an Asian logic foundry and wants global presence. U.S. OEMs value instant-on NV working memory that removes supercaps and batteries. A small partner can earn design-in services plus module margin, with capital limited to boards and inventory.

cards.why_it_could_work: FeFET puts the ferroelectric in the HKMG gate stack (sub-5nm films, low write energy), and FMC/GF integrated it on 28nm HKMG years ago. Embedded NVM below 28nm is scarce.

cards.name: SunRise-style 3D NOR 'quasi-volatile' memory as a DRAM substitute
cards.what_it_is: Thin-film 3D NOR charge-trap arrays with minutes-to-days retention, proposed by SunRise Memory (Eli Harari, San Jose) as a cheaper-than-DRAM tier refreshed rarely. A licensee would build it on NAND-class tooling.
cards.why_it_could_work: If 3D NOR offered DRAM-like latency at NAND-like cost per bit, it would sit under DRAM for AI/KV-cache capacity. SunRise has kept patenting into 2024-2026.

cards.name: Battery-free NV-cache / NVSRAM-replacement modules from off-the-shelf F-RAM
cards.what_it_is: Design and sell small U.S.-assembled modules and firmware drivers built on shipping Infineon EXCELON 4-16 Mb QSPI F-RAM (or RAMXEED FeRAM). They would be drop-in replacements for battery- or supercap-backed SRAM/NVSRAM write caches in industrial controllers, CNC and data loggers, including legacy-equipment repair.
cards.why_it_could_work: Shipping F-RAM offers 1e14 writes, zero write delay and >100-year retention, with no battery to fail, maintain or ship as hazmat. Legacy machines with battery-backed SRAM cards need maintenance-free replacements [ESTIMATE of demand]. Capital is just PCB design, contract EMS assembly and inventory. Key negative finding: F-RAM at ~$1-4/Mbit [ESTIMATE] is ~$8,000-30,000/GB, ~300-1,000x DDR5, so F-RAM cannot take DRAM sockets during the shortage, only battery-backed-SRAM sockets.

cards.name: U.S. independent emerging-memory test and qualification lab (HZO / IGZO / AlScN)
cards.what_it_is: An East Coast lab near Albany NanoTech or Philadelphia offering wafer-level ferroelectric and oxide-TFT characterization: P-E loops, wake-up/fatigue, retention bakes, PBTI/NBTI lifetime, coordination of radiation tests, and JEDEC-style qualification flows. Customers would be memory startups, university spinouts, SBIR performers and foreign memory firms entering the U.S.; it is a U.S. analogue of Neumonda's role for FMC.
cards.why_it_could_work: Reliability is the gating problem for every A1 device: imec IGZO PBTI ~1 yr vs a 5-yr target, HZO 1-month retention at 85C, NEO's claims company-reported only. FMC itself sold 'validation and qualification services' as part of its model and uses Neumonda's test platforms. Used parametric analyzers, probe stations and ferroelectric testers cost ~$0.3-1M [ESTIMATE].

cards.name: MemTech Atlas: emerging-memory device-parameter and $/GB cost-model data product
cards.what_it_is: A subscription web app that curates published device parameters (cell area, retention, endurance, layers, mask adders, demonstrated vs simulated) for IGZO/IWO, HZO, FeFET, AlScN, MRAM, ReRAM and 3D DRAM. It pairs them with an open, auditable $/GB cost model and a 'claims vs silicon' tracker, sold to memory investors, corporate strategy teams, defense program offices and procurement.
cards.why_it_could_work: It plays to the founder's software skill. This branch's research shows the data is scattered across press releases, IEDM/VLSI papers and paywalled TechInsights/Yole reports. Claims diverge sharply (NEO: 450 s simulated vs >1 s measured), and simple per-area analyses go viral (Kurnal Insights, Sep 2026). A transparent, cheaper tool for non-Yole budgets gives recurring revenue at ~80%+ margin.

cards.name: Onshore In-Ga-Zn oxide sputter-target and ALD-precursor supply for IGZO-channel DRAM
cards.what_it_is: Supply DRAM-grade IGZO/ITO/IWO sputter targets and indium/gallium/zinc ALD precursors to DRAM makers moving to oxide channels: Samsung 10a 4F2 VCT with a reportedly IGZO channel targeted for 2028, Kioxia OCTRAM, imec and IMECAS 3D 2T0C. U.S. research lines (Purdue ALD In2O3 on 200mm, NY CREATES) would be early customers, positioned as a non-Chinese indium chain.
cards.why_it_could_work: If oxide channels enter mainstream DRAM, every such wafer needs oxide-semiconductor deposition, and the materials play wins whichever cell architecture wins. Micron's U.S. fabs (Boise, Manassas, NY) and CHIPS-funded supply-chain localization favor onshore materials.
